scope: Proposition 5.10 (Small-spectrum bound) of the manuscript “The sharp singularity rate for biased symmetric sign matrices” (preprints/The-sharp-singularity-rate-for-biased-symmetric-sign-matrices-October-4-2026/biased-symmetric-sign-singularity.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 239 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 62c6a85b5437d9da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed ξ > 0, there is wξ > 0, depending also on p, such that typically a bit matrix B has at most ξN eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, in [−wξ √ N, wξ √ N]. Nonsingularity is not required. The exceptional probability is at most exp(−cp,ξN2).
